best_for: Network admins and home-lab owners who want a quick look at which hosts and ports answer on a subnet, without learning a full security scanner.

points.title: Quick sweeps of a network
points.text: It pings an IP range, random addresses or a list from a file, and checks ports on the hosts it finds. Results export to several formats, and a command-line mode suits scripts.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: It costs nothing and is released under the GPL 2.0.

points.title: Pick the Windows installer
points.text: The Windows installer bundles its own Java runtime and installs for the whole machine. The standalone .exe on the project site needs a separate 64-bit Java 21 or later.

points.title: Mac here lags behind
points.text: The project offers 3.12.2 for macOS 11 and later, with Java bundled, for Intel and Apple silicon. This site's Mac entry is 3.9.3, the release the project keeps for older macOS. Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Gatekeeper checks, so right-click and choose Open the first time.

points.title: Linux: community Flatpak or the .deb
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is 3.10.0, a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified, for x64 only. The project's own .deb and .rpm packages carry 3.12.2 and need Java 21 or later.

points.title: Very old Windows still covered
points.text: The project keeps version 2.21 for Windows 98, ME, 2000 and XP. It needs no installation.

points.title: Versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 7 versions. macOS and Linux list only one release, so downgrades there need another source.
